articles.title: Dow ends 400 points higher as investors buy AI stocks; Microsoft rallies
articles.description: Wall Street ended higher on Friday, lifted by Microsoft and other AI-related technology stocks, while high oil prices and a recent surge in US Treasury yields kept investors on edge.The S&P 500 gained 37.96 points, or 0.49%, to end at 7,742.09 points, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 125.51 points, or 0.47%, to 27,064.88. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 469.07 points, or 0.91%, to 51,819.05.Gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq capped a volatile week driven by uncertainty about what industries will win and lose from artificial intelligence, and by concerns about the US war with Iran and a surge in US Treasury yields.Microsoft rallied after the software giant unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent.Akamai Technologies surged after an $11.6 billion cloud services deal with AI leader Anthropic. The deal includes a warrant that could give Anthropic up to 5% of Akamai."That's a positive from the standpoint that people are still investing, deals are still being done," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments in Atlanta. "It's another circular deal, so OK ... but Akamai stock is up."Chip maker Qualcomm gained and Dell also advanced.Meta Platforms dipped. The social media company's stock has soared about 13% this week amid a strong reception to its Muse AI agent, which analysts say could benefit tech infrastructure stocks, while challenging banks, online shopping platforms and other consumer businesses.The S&P 500 this week has traded just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights are responsible for much of the recent increase in earnings expectations.A report that US and Iranian negotiators continued to explore a phased path out of the war, which would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade, helped market sentiment.Data also showed strong AI-related capital expenditures boosted demand for key manufactured capital goods, outpacing expectations in August.Brent crude eased but remained above $100 a barrel. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note hit a fresh 19-year high and was last up 3.4 basis points at 5.196%.Traders see a 66% chance of the Federal Reserve increasing interest rates by at least 25 basis points in October, up from around 50% earlier this week, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.US President Donald Trump said he had a "very productive meeting" with President Xi Jinping, following a three-day summit that showcased personal diplomacy rather than big breakthroughs in economic relations.Magazine publisher People Inc jumped after a report said MGM Resorts International was discussing a bid for the company.

articles.title: Best Financial Habits For Gen Z: Budgeting, Smart Investing & Money Tips | Personal Finance
articles.description: In this special edition of Money Today, we explore the Gen Z Investment Playbook with Pankaj Matpal, Founder and Managing Director of Optima Money Managers. From building healthy financial habits and starting investments early to managing expenses, avoiding unnecessary debt and planning for long-term goals, the discussion covers key aspects of personal finance for young investors. The conversation also explores the importance of budgeting, emergency funds, health insurance and disciplined investing. With easy access to financial information and a growing interest in newer asset classes, young investors face several opportunities and challenges. The episode highlights the need to balance present-day aspirations with future financial goals, understand investment risks and make informed decisions while building a sustainable approach to wealth creation.

articles.title: No coaching, full-time job at Google in Silicon Valley and $500K salary: How IIT alumnus Piyush Kapoor secured AIR 402 in UPSC CSE
articles.description: Piyush Kapoor, a Staff Software Engineer at Google in Mountain View, cleared the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2025 with AIR 402 on his fifth attempt while continuing to work full-time in Silicon Valley. Preparing from California, he studied two to three hours on weekdays and 13 to 14 hours over weekends despite the time difference with India. An IIT (BHU) Varanasi alumnus, Kapoor chose Mathematics as his optional subject and pursued civil services alongside his technology career.

articles.title: SHOCKING! India Home Loans Now CHEAPER Than US Mortgages: Historic 7.1% Vs 7.37% Reversal
articles.description: For the first time in modern economic history, home loans in India have turned cheaper than standard 30-year fixed mortgages in the United States! While average US mortgage rates have spiked back up to 7.37%, India’s baseline home loan rates are starting as low as 7.10%. In this special business report, we break down this unprecedented milestone. How did an emerging economy like India manage to offer lower borrowing costs than the world’s richest superpower? We analyse the contrasting post-Covid rate trajectories, from the aggressive stimulus and sticky inflation that pushed the US Federal Reserve into sharp rate hikes, to the disciplined monetary policy and external benchmark lending adopted by the Reserve Bank of India. Plus, hear what US Vice President J.D. Vance had to say about rising borrowing costs, housing affordability, and Washington’s pressure on the Fed to slash rates. Is this the new normal for global interest rates? What does it mean for middle-class homebuyers and real estate markets? Watch the full package to find out. Don't forget to Like, Share, and Subscribe for the latest business and financial news!
